messages.【問題点を短くまとめる決まり】PROJECT.md の issues を足す・変: [Rule for short issue summaries] When adding or changing issues in PROJECT.md, also update .ai/issues-summary.json in the same project (do not write to other projects). Format: {"items":[{"hash":"first 16 chars of the original's sha256","title":"issue name, up to 30 chars","state":"one of 未解決/確認待ち/判断待ち/解決済み/履歴","next":"next action, up to 50 chars (empty if none)","who":"one of 人/AI/empty"}]}. The original is the string as is, or text if it is an object. Compute hash with Node's require('node:crypto').createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('hex').slice(0, 16) (text is the original exactly; do not change spaces or line breaks). Do not put task IDs, commits, or test counts in the issue name or next action. When adding an item with a new state, set older items for the same issue to "履歴". Mark unverified things as "確認待ち"; do not assert bugs or fixes. Do not delete the original.

## Results and Storage
1. The originals of results are the extracted folders and source files. Create ZIPs and other archives just before distributing or sending, and don't keep them in deliverables after handing off.
2. Before saving anything new, compare its content (hash) with existing results. When bumping a version, move the old version to the Trash after saving and verifying.
3. For code already committed in main, don't also put file or ZIP copies in deliverables. Write the location and commit in the task file's "## 成果".
4. When finishing a task, write "## 成果" in the task file (format below). If there is nothing, write "- なし：" with the reason. Don't make the user choose by file name.

If there are only trivial changes, finish with the current assignee's self-check. Do not re-delegate for merging into main or publishing the same already-checked content and target, or for re-running read-only, diagnostic, or already-confirmed operations. Keep approvals for operations that need the user's approval. Check HEAD and unsaved changes, do the smallest implementation and save within the allowed scope, and record the tests and check results the change needs. Pass the check scope, diff, and verification results to claude・claude-fable-5-1 in the same task, and end your turn after delegating. Do not merge into main, push, or switch production.
Check → Report: independently verify the specified diff, impact scope, and existing verification results. If there are no new changes or problems, don't repeat tests; if nothing changed after the check, it also serves as the final review. Do not re-delegate for merging into main or publishing the same already-checked content and target, or for re-running read-only, diagnostic, or already-confirmed operations. ## Results and Storage
1. The source of truth for results is the unpacked folders and original files. Create ZIPs and other archives just before distributing or sending, and don't keep them in the results after handing them over.
2. Before saving something new, compare it with existing results by content (hash). Reuse a set only when relative layout, content, and permissions all match for every file; don't thin out identical files that are needed internally. When bumping a version, move the old version to Trash after saving and verifying.
3. For code already saved in main, don't put file or ZIP copies on top of it in the results. Write the location and commit in the task file's "## 成果".
4. When finishing a task, write "## 成果" in the task file (format below). If there is nothing, write "- なし：" with the reason. Don't make the user choose by file name.
5. Clean up to Trash only after results are saved and verified. Keep folders that contain unreceived content (also verify old handoffs, later additions, and hidden files). Never automatically delete original materials, other tasks' items, or the contents of dependency libraries.
6. Ask the user only for decisions: adopt or drop. For items whose content is unclear, the AI investigates first, then asks in everyday words.

### How to write "## 成果"
One item per line. Paths are relative to the ledger or main (main is body:, ledger is project:). Repositories saved in main are relative to main by default; main itself is . . In parentheses, write a short description for the user. Don't combine "なし" with other results. Write delegation acceptance, check results, and task progress in "## やったこと", not in "## 成果".
```
## 成果
- ファイル：作業/<作業ID>/確認結果.md (check results for the production screen)
- 本体保存済み：kosodate-qr@fe98eb8 (add adults when a child joins midway)
```
For check-only work:
```
## 成果
- なし：check only. Results are recorded in this task file
```
If there is no record of results, the AI investigates ownership, content, and what was already applied, and tidies the record. Don't ask the user to sort files. This shared rule takes priority over archiving instructions in older projects.

Whether something is trivial depends not on line count but on whether it leaves existing behavior, permissions, data structures, and external integrations unchanged with a clear impact scope. Call the Check assignee only when there are non-trivial changes, before high-impact operations, or when the user asks. When it applies, do one independent check. If fixes after the check are trivial, finish with the fixer's self-check and don't call the Check assignee again. However, still do individual checks for high-impact operations and rechecks the user asks for. Keep individual checks for high-impact operations such as publishing, authentication, money, and data deletion.
